episode.title: Deduplicate repository context files in nested linked worktrees
episode.before: At parent f9476a61e557bfdce2fbf3ffeaad0988fe47c184, project-context discovery resolved the configured working directory and walked every ancestor to the filesystem root. It deduplicated only identical path strings. When a linked worktree was nested beneath its main repository, the walk encountered a context file at the worktree root and the corresponding tracked file at the main-repository root, so both were loaded even though they represented duplicate repository instructions.
episode.after: At cced6a21da273b26ee4a23a803680614bbe8dd1e, context discovery reuses Git metadata resolution to identify a nested linked worktree, canonicalizes the worktree and common Git paths, verifies that the main repository is an ancestor with its own checked-out .git directory, and derives only the same-named main-root context file shadowed by the worktree-root file. The ancestor walk skips that exact file while preserving main-root inheritance when the worktree has no context, differently named context files, ancestors above the main repository, ordinary repositories, sibling worktrees, bare layouts, submodules, and invalid gitdir layouts.
episode.diff: The change exports the existing GitPaths type and findGitPaths function from the Git footer module; adds findShadowedContextFile to the resource loader using canonical paths, Git common-directory topology, ancestor containment, checked-out-main-repository verification, and filename matching; consults the derived path during the existing ancestor walk and excludes only that path; and adds nine focused regression tests covering the duplicate case and preservation boundaries.

evidence_units.claim: The pinned commit is cced6a21da273b26ee4a23a803680614bbe8dd1e with parent f9476a61e557bfdce2fbf3ffeaad0988fe47c184 and subject "fix(coding-agent): stop loading AGENTS.md twice in nested git worktrees (#7221)".
evidence_units.source: git show --format=fuller cced6a21da273b26ee4a23a803680614bbe8dd1e; issue-bundle.json resolved_commit and parent_commit

evidence_units.claim: Before the change, loadProjectContextFiles walked from resolvedCwd to the filesystem root, loaded one preferred context file per directory, and suppressed only paths already present in seenPaths; it had no Git-worktree-aware shadow detection.

The existing findGitPaths routine walks upward for .git metadata and resolves repoDir, commonGitDir, and HEAD for ordinary repositories, linked worktrees using gitdir and commondir files, and gitdir-style layouts without commondir. The commit exports this routine and its result type for reuse.

findShadowedContextFile canonicalizes commonGitDir and repoDir, derives mainRepoRoot from the common Git directory, requires the worktree root to be nested under that root, and requires mainRepoRoot/.git to canonicalize to commonGitDir. These guards exclude ordinary repositories, sibling worktrees, bare containers, and submodule metadata layouts.

Shadow detection activates only when the worktree root contains a loadable context file and returns the main-repository-root path with the same basename, so a missing worktree context preserves inheritance and a differently named main-root context remains loadable.
evidence_units.source: git show cced6a21da273b26ee4a23a803680614bbe8dd1e:packages/coding-agent/src/core/resource-loader.ts, final two statements of findShadowedContextFile

evidence_units.claim: The ancestor walk now computes one shadowedContextFile before traversal, canonicalizes each discovered context path for comparison, and excludes only the matching shadowed file; its traversal, ordering, and seen-path behavior otherwise remain unchanged.

DefaultResourceLoader reloads project context by calling loadProjectContextFiles with its current cwd and agentDir unless context loading is disabled, so the worktree-aware filtering affects the normal resource-loading path.

candidate_atomics.name: classify-nested-linked-worktree-shadow
candidate_atomics.title: Identify the exact main-repository context shadowed by a nested worktree
candidate_atomics.description: Resolve repository metadata and filesystem identity to determine whether the current checkout is a linked worktree nested beneath its checked-out main repository, then derive the same-named main-root context path only when the worktree root supplies its own context.

semantic_action.intent: Determine whether ancestor traversal would encounter one duplicate repository-context file caused by a nested linked-worktree layout.
semantic_action.pre_state: A context loader has a working directory that may be inside an ordinary repository, linked worktree, bare-worktree layout, submodule, malformed Git layout, or no repository.
semantic_action.post_state: The resolver returns exactly one canonical shadowed ancestor path only for a linked worktree nested under its checked-out main repository with a worktree-root context file; otherwise it returns no shadow candidate.
semantic_action.validation: Construct representative Git metadata layouts and verify positive classification only for the nested linked-worktree duplicate case, with no candidate for ordinary, sibling, bare, submodule, missing-context, or invalid-gitdir cases.

candidate_atomics.name: exclude-only-shadowed-context-during-ancestor-walk
candidate_atomics.title: Skip only the shadowed context while preserving ancestor inheritance
candidate_atomics.description: Integrate the resolved shadow path into the existing ancestor traversal, compare canonical paths, and omit only the duplicate while retaining ordering, unrelated ancestors, differently named files, and fallback behavior.

semantic_action.intent: Prevent duplicate repository instructions without weakening normal hierarchical context inheritance.
semantic_action.pre_state: Ancestor discovery may include a worktree-root context and an exact main-root shadow candidate while also containing legitimate global, outer-ancestor, or differently named context files.
semantic_action.post_state: The loaded context sequence excludes the exact shadowed main-root file and preserves every other context file in the existing outer-to-inner ordering.
semantic_action.validation: Assert the duplicate case returns one worktree context, then assert inheritance and boundary cases retain main-root, outer-ancestor, differently named, bare-container, sibling, submodule, ordinary-repository, and malformed-layout contexts.

candidate_workflows.name: deduplicate-context-across-nested-worktree-and-main-root
candidate_workflows.title: Remove duplicate context loading in a nested linked worktree
candidate_workflows.description: Resolve the actual repository/worktree topology before ancestor traversal, identify only the main-root context shadowed by the nested worktree copy, and filter that one path while preserving established inheritance semantics.

workflow_graph.goal: Load repository instructions once when a linked worktree is physically nested beneath its main repository, without dropping legitimate ancestor context in other layouts.
when_to_use: A resource loader walks filesystem ancestors and loads context files from multiple directory levels.
A linked worktree can be located beneath its main repository, causing both worktree-root and main-root copies of the same tracked context filename to appear in one ancestor chain.
anti_goals: Do not stop traversal at the repository or worktree root.
Do not globally deduplicate files by content, inode, or filename alone.
Do not suppress context belonging to directories above the main repository.
Do not reinterpret bare-worktree containers, sibling worktrees, or submodule superprojects as duplicate main-repository roots.
not_applicable_when: Context discovery does not walk beyond the checkout root.
The duplicated resource is not attributable to a nested linked-worktree and checked-out-main-repository relationship.
Repository metadata and the before/after behavior cannot be established.
inputs: Git repository metadata including gitdir and optional commondir
existing ancestor traversal and ordering contract
workflow_graph.entry_state: The loader performs an unrestricted ancestor walk and may load both a nested worktree's context and its main repository's same-named tracked context.
workflow_graph.exit_state: The exact main-root context shadowed by a nested worktree-root context is omitted, while all non-shadowed contexts and existing traversal ordering remain intact.

steps.condition: Run before ancestor filtering whenever project context discovery is enabled.
steps.validation: The classifier yields the same-named main-root path only for a nested linked worktree backed by a checked-out main repository, and yields no candidate for preserved layouts.

steps.condition: Apply the exclusion only when classification returned a shadowed path; otherwise retain the original ancestor walk unchanged.
steps.validation: The positive regression returns only worktree instructions, while all inheritance and topology boundary tests preserve their expected context sequences.

validation_ladder: Verify the parent implementation lacks topology-aware shadow detection and can admit both nested paths.
Test the positive nested-worktree case with same-named context files at worktree and main roots.
Test filename and absence branches: preserve main-root inheritance when the worktree has no context and preserve differently named main-root context.
Test topology exclusions: bare layout, sibling worktree, submodule, and ordinary repository.
Test traversal boundaries: preserve ancestors above the main repository and continue normally when gitdir metadata is invalid.
Run the focused resource-loader test file in an environment with the repository's Node.js toolchain.
stop_conditions: Stop without filtering when Git paths cannot be resolved.
Stop without filtering when the worktree root is not physically below the derived main-repository root.
Stop without filtering when the derived main root is not a checked-out repository whose .git directory is the common Git directory.
Stop without filtering when the worktree root has no context file to shadow the main-root file.
